headline: 255 votes: Mirza Fakhrul elected as president of Bangladesh
summary: The BNP candidate secured a decisive victory in the parliamentary vote, defeating Oli Ahmed with 88 votes.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 24th President of Bangladesh, securing 255 votes in a parliamentary election. His opponent, Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, received 88 votes.

The election took place on Thursday in the National Parliament, where 343 out of 349 eligible members voted. Six members did not cast their votes, including independent MP Rumin Farhana and several BNP members who were abroad or receiving medical treatment.

Following the announcement of the result by Chief Election Commissioner A.M.M. Nasir Uddin, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the new president with a red rose. The event was marked by a display of unity, with Mirza Fakhrul embracing members of the opposition.
The presidency became vacant after President Mohammed Sahabuddin resigned on July 24 for health reasons. Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed had been serving as the acting president since then.
The Election Commission has issued a gazette notification officially declaring Mirza Fakhrul as the president. He is scheduled to take the oath of office on Friday evening.
International congratulations have already poured in for the new president, including messages from the United Kingdom and China, as well as from Professor Yunus and other political leaders.

headline_marked: England lead by 195 runs as [[Brook scores quickfire 91]] against Pakistan
headline: England lead by 195 runs as Brook scores quickfire 91 against Pakistan
summary: Harry Brook punished a costly drop to strengthen England's grip on the first Test at Headingley, leaving Pakistan in a precarious position.
details: England reached 366-8 at the end of a rain-affected second day, holding a commanding 195-run lead over Pakistan's first-innings total of 171.
Harry Brook played a pivotal role with a quickfire 91, capitalizing on a dropped catch by Pakistan captain Salman Ali Agha at second slip early in his innings.
Captain Joe Root scored 66, while Jordan Cox made 73 and Dan Lawrence added 51, with several England batsmen falling just short of centuries.
Jordan Cox and Joe Root shared a strong third-wicket partnership of 150 runs before falling in quick succession.
For Pakistan, spinner Ali Usman was the standout performer, claiming his maiden five-wicket haul with figures of 5-92 in 23 overs.
England's dominance began on Wednesday when pacemen Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue shared all 10 Pakistan wickets between them to bowl the visitors out for 171.
caption:
A costly drop and a dominant batting display! England now lead by 195 runs in the first Test against Pakistan.

England reached 366-8 at the end of a rain-affected second day, holding a commanding 195-run lead over Pakistan's first-innings total of 171.

Harry Brook played a pivotal role with a quickfire 91, capitalizing on a dropped catch by Pakistan captain Salman Ali Agha at second slip early in his innings.

Captain Joe Root scored 66, while Jordan Cox made 73 and Dan Lawrence added 51, with several England batsmen falling just short of centuries.

Jordan Cox and Joe Root shared a strong third-wicket partnership of 150 runs before falling in quick succession.

For Pakistan, spinner Ali Usman was the standout performer, claiming his maiden five-wicket haul with figures of 5-92 in 23 overs.

England's dominance began on Wednesday when pacemen Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue shared all 10 Pakistan wickets between them to bowl the visitors out for 171.
